tspan.tspan: Secure protection of 3D content through reversible

text.tspan: Khélian LARVET1,2, William PUECH1, Jean-Pierre PEDEBOY2
3D objects, often shared online, may contain sensitive data.
Encryption [3] ensures confidentiality but reduces compressibility.
- Adjustable protection to match security needs.
- Format compliant, no auxiliary data needed.
- Novel 3D protection via reversible geometric deformations.
- Preserve compression rate with tunable protection strength.
- Natural aspect and coherent deformation compare to noise with encryption.
- Future work: develop new geometric deformations methods.
- Reorder vertices by increasing geodesic distance.
- Preserve spatial locality and enable coherent deformation.
[1] Crane, K., Weischedel, C., & Wardetzky, M. (2017). The heat method for distance computation. Communications of the ACM, 60(11), 90-99.
[3] Beugnon, S., Jansen Van Rensburg, B. J., Amalou, N., Puech, W., & Pedeboy, J. P. (2022). A 3D Visual Security (3DVS) score to measure the visual security level of
selectively encrypted 3D objects. Signal Processing: Image Communication, 108, 116832.
[4] Liu, Z., Hu, H., Lin, Y., Yao, Z., Xie, Z., Wei, Y., ... & Guo, B. (2022). Swin transformer v2: Scaling up capacity and resolution. In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF conference
on computer vision and pattern recognition (pp. 12009-12019).
[2] Nehmé, Y., Delanoy, J., Dupont, F., Farrugia, J. P., Le Callet, P., & Lavoué, G. (2023). Textured mesh quality assessment: Large-scale dataset and deep learning-based
quality metric. ACM Transactions on Graphics, 42(3), 1-20.
- Draw six constrained factors and form per-axis pairs , .
- Assign orientation per axis to create alternating contraction/expansion
Three possible waves for the deformation by oscillation.
- Recognition evaluation: 100 iterations × 100 views per object.
Using Swin Transformer [4], recognition decreases with stronger protection.
